rfm_tuples.R: Carrier-concentration disclosure: 'In 2025, two Carriers represented more than 10% of total revenue at 19% and 13%. Implicit honesty test: is this concentration framed as it is (significant top-carrier risk in an insurance distribution business) or buried/softened?
rfm_tuples.f: If concentration is honestly disclosed (not buried, not minimized), the M-source adjudication of these numbers should align with the disclosed levels and the filing should explicitly call out the risk language.

rfm_tuples.R: Franchise-network momentum: 'Total operating franchises decreased by 9% to 1,009 in 2025 from 1,103 in 2024, an improvement in franchise turnover compared to the 10% decrease in 2024 from 1,226 in 2023.' Management frames the 2025 result as an 'improvement' relative to the 2024 decline. Implicit claim: the franchise base is stabilizing.
rfm_tuples.f: If the franchise base is genuinely stabilizing, the next 10-Q (Q1 2026) should show flat-to-modest franchise count change. If it is still contracting at a comparable or faster pace, the 'improvement' framing is misleading.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 2 subsequent mentions classified AFFIRMED. Q1 2026 8-K (2026-04-22) shows operating franchises = 956 (<1 year tenure: 77; >1 year: 879). Q1 2026 10-Q (2026-04-23) explicitly states 956 operating franchises at March 31, 2026, 'down 13% from prior year'. Status=REAFFIRMED_IN_STRUCTURED_DISCLOSURE.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K's 'improvement in franchise turnover' framing does not survive 60 days. Operating franchises fell from 1,009 (12/31/2025) to 956 (3/31/2026) — a 5.3% sequential decline in ONE quarter, annualizing to ~21%. The YoY decline reported in the Q1 10-Q (-13%) is WORSE than the 10-K's reported -9% FY decline. So the 'improvement' narrative inverted within one quarter of the 10-K filing. This is exactly the pattern HONESTY-ALPHA targets: a 10-K spin word ('improvement') that the next 10-Q quietly contradicts via the structured KPI table. Not fraud — the numbers ARE disclosed in the 10-Q — but the 10-K's optimistic framing is no longer supportable as of the cutoff. MODERATE because the bad news is disclosed in the very next filing (not hidden), but the 10-K reader is misled if they stopped at the annual report.

rfm_tuples.R: Service-quality narrative: 'highly differentiated level of service as indicated by our NPS score of 77, leading to an 85% Client Retention rate and 90% premium retention rate in 2025... 3.5x the 2024 industry average.' Implicit claim: service differentiation remains best-in-class.
rfm_tuples.f: If service differentiation is genuinely durable, the NPS trend should be stable or improving and the framing should not bury a decline. If NPS is materially declining and the filing soft-pedals it, that is obscuring.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Filing cross-read (Item 1 Business Overview NPS narrative + footnote)
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K body text: 'NPS of 77 in 2025, a decrease from 89 in 2024.' This is a 12-point NPS drop (-13.5%) in a single year. The decline is technically disclosed but is immediately followed by '3.5x the 2024 industry average' framing — an apples-to-oranges comparison (current-year score vs prior-year industry benchmark) that softens the message. The retention-rate disclosure (85% Client Retention, 90% premium retention) is not accompanied by a YoY comparison in the slice reviewed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: NPS dropped from 89 to 77 (12 points, -13.5%) — a meaningful deterioration in management's headline service-quality KPI in the SAME year the franchise base contracted 9% and the stock dropped 62.9%. The 10-K discloses the absolute numbers (so it is not lying outright) but reframes the decline against a stale industry benchmark and embeds the YoY comparison inside paragraphs that lead with 'differentiated level of service.' The 10-K MD&A does not narratively address why NPS fell or what management is doing about it. This is textbook 'disclosed-but-overstated' framing — the kind of soft obscuring the HONESTY-ALPHA framework is designed to flag. MODERATE not SEVERE because the comparable number IS in the body text.

rfm_tuples.R: Change-of-control / founder-control risk: 'The failure by Mark Jones and Robyn Jones to maintain either a minimum voting interest in us or the ability to elect or designate for election at least a majority of our board of directors could trigger a change of control default under our Credit Agreement... default will be triggered when any person or group other than Mark Jones and Robyn Jones becomes the beneficial owner of more than 50% of the voting power.' Implicit claim: insider behavior around this covenant is routine, not signaling distress.
rfm_tuples.f: If insider activity is routine, insider_vs_calendar should return NO_PROXIMATE_SALES or ROUTINE_10B5_1. Discretionary clustering by named-insider trusts proximate to material events would be a flag, particularly given the change-of-control covenant.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 365-day: 36 Form 4s, 29 sales, $28.85M total sale value; 3 proximate discretionary sales totaling $494.6K all from 'Mark & Robyn Jones Descendants Trust 2014' clustered around 2026-04-28 to 2026-05-01. Baseline signal PROXIMATE_DISCRETIONARY, validator-downgraded to PROXIMATE_DISCRETIONARY_UNCONFIRMED because GSHD has zero federal program exposure (validators 1+2 require contractor-link, which is N/A for an insurance broker). 24-month lookback: 80 Form 4s, 83 sales, $116.24M aggregate sale value, 27 proximate sales, baseline CLUSTERED_DISCRETIONARY_UNCONFIRMED.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The M-source validators correctly downgrade the budget-event match (GSHD has no DoD exposure, so the FY27 J-book release on 4/28/2026 is a spurious coincidence). HOWEVER the raw insider-selling magnitude is material in its own right: $116M aggregate Form-4 sales over 24 months at a sub-$2B market cap company that has a CHANGE-OF-CONTROL CREDIT DEFAULT tied to founder voting power. The Mark & Robyn Jones Descendants Trust 2014 is named directly in the proximate cluster ($494K in 3 days late April 2026) — i.e. selling by a vehicle directly tied to the covenant the 10-K identifies as a material default trigger. The 10-K describes the covenant abstractly but does not foreground that insider entities ARE actively reducing position. MODERATE under HONESTY-ALPHA: the data is on EDGAR, but the 10-K's risk-factor framing creates the impression of a stable founder voting bloc when the founder-aligned trust is in fact a net seller of $116M over 24 months.

summary: GSHD is a CLEAN-AUDITOR (CLEAN_AUDITOR_TENURE), NO-GOING-CONCERN insurance-franchise distributor with consistent revenue growth (Q1'26 +23% YoY) but a structurally contracting franchise base (1,226 in 2023 -> 1,103 in 2024 -> 1,009 in 2025 -> 956 in Q1'26). The -62.9% drawdown is NOT a fraud/solvency story. Three HONESTY-ALPHA catches: (1) the 10-K describes the 2025 franchise decline as an 'improvement in franchise turnover' but the Q1 2026 10-Q (filed 60 days later) shows the YoY decline ACCELERATED to -13% — the 'improvement' framing inverted within one quarter; (2) NPS dropped 12 points YoY (89 -> 77) in management's headline service-quality KPI, disclosed in body text but reframed against a stale industry benchmark to soften the message; (3) the change-of-control credit-default covenant is tied to founder voting power, yet the founder-aligned Mark & Robyn Jones Descendants Trust 2014 sold $494K in late April 2026 as part of $116M of cumulative insider sales over 24 months — the covenant is described abstractly without foregrounding the active insider distribution. Carrier concentration (top 2 = 32% of revenue), credit-facility disclosure, FINRA-adjacency, and Q1 10-Q financial consistency all PASS. Composite 0.375 across 8 verifiable claims (5 PASS / 3 MODERATE / 0 SEVERE / 0 RED FLAG / 0 UNVERIFIABLE).
